clue.text: The keycard shakes in her hand; she drops it twice.
The door chain on, seven times.
Pollen on a dark sleeve. Her glasses fog, then clear.
A game show, loud.
Whispers into the phone: "Is she eating?"
An envelope under the main door. She stares at it and leaves it till 02:30.
Ink on her fingertips; she scrubs at the sink.
A tube of rolled leaflets.
The river report.
Folds a paper boat and sets it on the sill. Two now.
A white catering jacket flecked with gold; a badge reading "J."
Pours a miniature into the sink; writes "400" on the notepad.
A black-and-white film.
A voice memo; the words are lost.
Red clay on his collar and knees.
Kit laid out in order; the bedspread folded back a hand's width.
Reads his daughter chapter one of The Lamplighter's Mouse. "I know. Papa's late."
The news, muted.
Grease under her nails.
Three laptops in one bag.
Chess by phone: "e4."
Dry cereal from the box.
Salt rime on her boots; she smells her gloves.
White gloves on before she touches the lamp.
A flat portfolio.
Paints the river and pins it up.
An art auction channel.
A photocopied page, read under the lamp with a magnifier.
A miniature into the sink; "401" on the notepad.
A film.
Steadier on the keycard.
An orchid in her buttonhole.
The chain on, seven times.
Presses the orchid in the hotel directory.
A suit, not his kit.
A laminated pass on a lanyard: "BH".
Reads chapter two.
Irons tomorrow's shirt.
Grease under her nails again.
A spool of cable.
She opens the door a crack; an envelope.
Counts cash, hands shaking.
Chess by phone: "Nf3."
A coil of blue rope.
Rope burn across one palm.
The river report.
Boat three on the sill.
A cut palm, bandaged.
Red clay on her boots and on the white gloves: the same red as 401's collar.
A brass tag, "BH-0611", set on the sill.
She does not paint. She sits awake.
Dials a number from a card, "Friends of the River". It rings out; she writes it again.
Boat four.
The room phone rings; she answers, hears a voice, hangs up.
Sits with her hand on the receiver.
"Chapter three. The mouse climbs the tower." Reads it to the end.
Kit in order.
Opens to the stranger; a cream envelope.
A photograph on the desk, face up, then face down: 403's guest at her own door.
Reads a printed list; stops on one line.
Dials the room phone: "Ruthie, it's—"
Sets the receiver down very slowly.
Chess: "Bb5."
"Then who is the source?" Slams the receiver.
The miniature; "402".
A film, sound off.
The game show turned up.
Whispers to her neighbour under the noise.
Knits.
A flat hard case under the bed, where there was nothing last night.
Leaves a message: "It's with me. It's heavier than it should be."
Gloves on; paints.
Runs a gloved hand along the case's back.
Lew the porter at the door, with an iron.
Reads chapter four.
Irons; folds.
A man at the door says "hotel security". It is 401.
A card left on the table: "Corvane Risk".
She shuts two laptops at once.
404 at her door.
She unscrews a knitting needle's end; it is hollow.
She gives the needle to him.
The miniature; "403".
A knitting needle on the desk.
The stranger at the door.
Drops an envelope of money in the bin; at 02:40 takes it out.
Two pairs of feet, bare and in slippers; two people sit down on the floor.
A photograph slid across the floor between them.
Room service: a pot of tea.
The case open on the desk; she peels the painting's backing.
Folded pages inside; she reads them with gloves on.
Paints, but the picture is of the room.
Drinks the miniature. Does not write "404". Voice memo: "Day four hundred and four. I'm sorry."
A press card on the bed: "J. FERRER".
A business card: "wine salesman".
To the mirror, until her voice holds: "I kept the accounts. I kept two sets."
To the mirror: "My name is Ines Maro."
A lanyard: "conference interpreter".
Reads chapter five; after she hangs up, says "No" to the photograph.
A postcard to his daughter, signed "T. Vell".
An insurance assessor's folder.
Sews the last letter of the banner; talks to the river report about her father.
A letter from her group: "Dear Ruth".
A nurse's watch pinned to her coat.
Records a message she does not send.
"It's Kit. Kit Saelens. Your sister. Remember her?"
A student card.
Copies the folded pages by hand at the desk, all night.
A luggage label: "M. LINDE".
The same label, second line: "restorer".
Boat seven, the last on the sill.
The banner, rolled and tied with the blue rope.
The chain on, seven times.
A letter from "Ashdown Relocation" on the bed.
A woman answers: "She's asleep." He sits on the bed for a long time.
He leaves by the main door. The room is empty till 01:55.
A Courant envelope, the booking confirmation inside.
An empty notepad.
Her screen shows a job board, handle "LANTERN".
Chess; she loses on purpose.
401 at her door; she lets him in. She shows him the folded pages. At 01:55 he leaves without the case.
The stranger; an envelope: payment, and "the service stair, 05:30 Monday".
An "Abbot Fine Art" invoice.
Waits by the door in her coat.
Leaves with 404.
Back at 02:50 with ink on her hands.
Ruth, soaked from the river.
Kit holds her hands under the hot tap.
The two of them sit on the floor of 406. The towel is gone.
Takes the needle from the desk.
Does not touch the minibar.
Leaves.
Back at 02:50 with ink on his hands.
Irons a shirt.
Reads chapter six.
Packs his kit.
Leaves.
Back at 03:30 without his kit.
Paints, all night.

office_clues.text: Six guest cards, one line each: 401 a soldier for hire, 402 a whistleblower, 403 an art thief, 404 an undercover journalist, 405 a hacker, 406 an activist.
Evening paper: the Glasshouse late opening ends 23:00.
Evening paper: the Printworks night run ends 23:30.
Evening paper: the Assembly Rooms gala rehearsal ends 00:30.
Evening paper: fish market trade ends 02:15.
Lew: "Nowhere in this town's more than half an hour from here."
Evening paper: "Orchid week at the Glasshouse".
The night strip of night one.
Lew at the hand-over: "Stair door's locked from your side. Someone's idea."
The chute ends in a steel box: a brass plate "W", "2:14" chalked on the lid.
Abel Fenn's log, last season: six other guests, the same columns, a 2:14 column every night. Last page: "I stopped writing it down."
The night strip of night three.
Evening paper: "Courant drops river warehouse story".

The booking ledger: six rooms booked by Corvane Risk (401), Ashdown Relocation (402), Abbot Fine Art (403), The Evening Courant (404), LANTERN (405), Friends of the River (406); one payer, Wren Holdings, account ending 0214.
Behind the ledger: your own hiring papers, and a sheet headed "Product: night log. Client: D."

false_signs.starts: The night after a guest is exposed (suspicion 100): one staged beat a night, in the window of the beat it replaces.
false_signs.tell: Staged facing the rose: the clue card's sketch shows the guest's eyes on the viewer. A second look shows the conflict.

none.reason: 406's lens is covered by script from 01:00 and the gap never raises suspicion, so nothing is staged to the lens.

Lew at the door with a pot of tea.
She hands her visitor a business card.
Room service leaves an iron.
Holds up a photograph from the envelope.
An envelope of cash left on the table.
A business card: "wine salesman".

A lanyard: "conference interpreter".
A nurse's watch pinned to her coat.
A card: "restorer".
A Courant envelope on the desk.
A "Friends of the River" card on the bed.
A "Corvane Risk" card.

A letter from "Ashdown Relocation".
